articles.title: ‘He was all fire’: brilliant Bacio blasts to Nunthorpe Stakes success at York
articles.summary: Jockey Juan Hernandez dashes to airport after victory. ‘He’s just so fast that it doesn’t matter what he runs on’ His name is the Italian for a kiss but there is little delicacy or tenderness about Bacio, the front-running winner of the Nunthorpe Stakes here on Friday.
body: Juan Hernandez, Bacio’s jockey, had a plane to catch later on Friday – he has booked rides in California on Saturday afternoon – and his mount did all he could to ensure that he got to Heathrow on time, producing a carbon copy of his win in a five-furlong handicap at Royal Ascot in June.

The going at Ascot was good-to-firm and much energy had been expended in the run-up to Friday’s race on speculation over Bacio’s ability to handle softer ground. As it turned out, it made no difference at all to Wesley Ward’s colt, and the American trainer finally has a Nunthorpe success to go with his 13 wins at Royal Ascot since 2009.

Ward was on the Knavesmire to watch his three previous Nunthorpe runners but followed Friday’s race from his barn at Keeneland in Kentucky, the venue for this year’s Breeders’ Cup meeting in late October.

“I know a lot of people were worried about the ground for him, but he didn’t know that,” Hernandez said, before running to a waiting helicopter to connect with the 6.15pm flight from Heathrow to Los Angeles.

articles.title: Ex-England bowler Cross to retire at end of summer
articles.summary: Former England bowler Kate Cross, praised for her "incredible contribution" to the women's game, to retire from cricket at the end of the summer.
body: The 34-year-old, who played 102 times for England between 2013 and 2025, has been playing in domestic cricket since losing her England contract last year.

"It is incredibly hard to imagine ever saying goodbye to playing the sport that has been such a huge part of my life and shaped me into the person I am today but the final chapter is in sight," Cross said.
"I feel so fortunate to have had the opportunity to play the game I love professionally and get to do it at the highest level."

Dame Sarah Storey, the chair of Lancashire where Cross made her debut aged 14 and became the first woman on the county's academy, described Cross as a "true Lancashire legend", adding she "made an incredible contribution to both Lancashire and England Women".

articles.title: Tour of Britain Women: Kim Le Court storms to stage three win and overall lead
articles.summary: Mauritian rider bursts clear on final climb of Great Orme. Le Court leads GC standings with two stages remaining. Mauritius’s Kim Le Court powered to victory in stage three of the Tour of Britain in Llandudno and moved top of the general classification.
body: The 30-year-old AG Insurance-Soudal rider attacked with 2.5km to go on the 104.7km route from Mold to cross the summit finish on Great Orme 13 seconds ahead of Germany’s Liane Lippert (Movistar).
Le Court burst clear on the final climb and the Netherlands’ overnight GC leader, Lorena Wiebes, who had won the first two stages, could not respond.
Sweden’s Caroline Andersson (Liv AlUla Jayco) finished third a further seven seconds behind, while Britain’s Lauren Dickson (FDJ United – SUEZ) was sixth as Wiebes came home in 10th.
Le Court now leads the GC table with two days remaining, 26 seconds ahead of Lippert and with a 35-second advantage over third-placed Wiebes.

articles.title: Jannik Sinner ‘very sad and disappointed’ as knee injury puts him out of US Open
articles.summary: World No 1 makes ‘difficult decision’ to miss slam. ‘New York has a special place in my heart’ Jannik Sinner will miss the US Open with a right knee injury. The world No 1 has not played a match since beating Alexander Zverev last month to successfully defend his Wimbledon title, missing the…
body: The news comes a day after his great rival Carlos Alcaraz, whom the Italian lost to in the final in New York 12 months ago, revealed he will make his comeback at Flushing Meadows after four months out with a wrist injury.

Sinner said: “Even though I have been working hard with my team and my medical staff, we have now had to make the difficult decision that I will not be able to compete at the US Open this year. We have been back on court in Monte Carlo over the last couple of days and have realised that I still need more time to recover from my right knee issue.

“I’m obviously very sad and disappointed, as New York has a special place in my heart. I was very much looking forward to coming back and playing in the electric atmosphere in front of the great fans there.”

It will be the first grand slam the 25-year-old has missed since making his debut at the US Open in 2019 and will further focus attention on the physical demands of the tennis calendar. He is the sixth man to withdraw from the singles since the entry list was announced, while six women have also pulled out, including Britain’s Emma Raducanu.

articles.title: What does Heggebo's deception ban mean for football?
articles.summary: BBC Sport explores the fallout from the decision to ban West Brom striker Aune Heggebo for two matches for "successfully deceiving a match official".
body: It is 0-0 between Norwich City and West Bromwich Albion with 15 minutes remaining in the opening game of the season at Carrow Road.
Baggies forward Jimmy Jay-Morgan crosses it into Norwich's six-yard box at pace, flying by the outstretched hand of Canaries keeper Vladan Kovacevic and into the path of Albion striker Aune Heggebo.
The Norwegian jumps, seemingly trying to guide it in with his foot but it hits his hand instead and flies into the net.
Did he mean to handball it? Hard to tell at the speed it all happened.

articles.title: Darryl Strawberry Urges Support for Nick Kyrgios After Cocaine Suspension: ‘He Just Needs Time’
articles.summary: Darryl Strawberry is urging people not to write off Nick Kyrgios after the tennis star tested positive for a cocaine metabolite and was provisionally suspended,...
body: Speaking to TMZ Sports, the former MLB star argued that Kyrgios needs support while he deals with the consequences of the positive test. “He just needs time,” Strawberry said, adding that Kyrgios needs “people to love him through the process.”

Kyrgios provided a sample during an ATP 250 event in Mallorca on June 22. A World Anti-Doping Agency-accredited laboratory confirmed benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine, in the sample on July 17, according to the International Tennis Integrity Agency. His mandatory provisional suspension has been in effect since Aug. 4.

Kyrgios acknowledged the positive test publicly on Aug. 19, calling it a “huge mistake” and accepting full responsibility. He also said years of injuries had taken a physical and mental toll and announced that he would spend 28 days away from social media and public life while focusing on himself.

Strawberry told TMZ that his reaction comes from experiencing public judgment during his own struggles with drugs. He argued that athletic success does not prevent someone from struggling privately and cautioned against reducing people to the problems they experience away from competition.

articles.title: FIFA hit Argentina star with 10-Match ban as four World Cup finalists punished
articles.summary: FIFA has suspended Argentina pair Leandro Paredes and Nahuel Molina for their roles in the melee that erupted following the World Cup Final. Paredes has received a substantial 10-game suspension, while Nahuel Molina has been issued a seven-game ban.
body: Paredes and Molina both drew particular scrutiny for their actions after Argentina suffered a 1-0 defeat to Spain in the final in New York.
Paredes was captured on video seizing Eric Garcia by the neck and tossing Gavi to the turf. Molina was observed hitting Rodri as he rushed to celebrate.

Former Argentina legend Roberto Ayala, who now serves on his nation's coaching staff, was also implicated in the post-game incidents and has received a three-game suspension, while Spain midfielder Gavi has been forced to accept a one-game ban, as per The Mirror.

FIFA has also imposed a $121,000 fine on the Argentina FA after their players showed a Falklands banner following their semi-final victory over England and for discrimination and racist conduct by supporters.

articles.title: Chelsea to host Shakhtar's Champions League home games amid ongoing exile
articles.summary: Shakhtar Donetsk will play their Champions League home games at Stamford Bridge this season after coming to an agreement with Chelsea to host their European matches while they remain in exile from their Donbas Arena home.
body: The Ukrainian side had been looking for a new temporary base for their continental games and had been linked with holding them at Brentford's Gtech Community Stadium, but will instead travel several miles towards central London to Chelsea's 40,044-capacity home.

At the time of the last UK census in 2021, an estimated 19,000 Ukrainians lived in London while around 45,000 have since arrived in the capital since the Russian invasion of Ukraine began in 2022 with a high proportion settled in west London where Stamford Bridge is located.
The stadium will host at least four matches with Shakhtar automatically qualifying for the league phase of this season's competition after winning the Ukrainian Premier League last season.

Chelsea pointed to their own "disappointing 2025/26 season" as helping them with the logistics of accommodating Shakhtar, as their own 10th-placed finish in the Premier League means they will not be playing European football this season.

articles.title: Doyle: Ebor test should suit Klassleader
articles.summary: Sky Sports Racing ambassador Hollie Doyle shares her expert views on the best of the action at York and Chester on Saturday, including the £500,000 Ebor Handicap.
body: If you're willing to forgive his run in the Old Newton Cup at Newmarket last month then Klassleader must be on your shortlist for the £500,000 Sky Bet Ebor Handicap (3.35) at York on Saturday.

My husband Tom (Marquand) felt he simply didn't handle the undulations that day but the way he justified favouritism in a mile and a half handicap at this track back in May gives me the impression he's well treated on a mark of 98.

Alan King's Daiquiri Bay had his moment in the sun in the Copper Horse Stakes at Royal Ascot and looks sure to go well over this extra quarter mile. He's no stranger to The Knavesmire, having finished a gallant third over course and distance in last season's Melrose Stakes, and has been handed a good low draw.

Another open to improvement is the Willie Mullins runner Love Me Tender, a fascinating recruit from Germany who has winning form in soft ground. That said, William Buick's mount has something to prove on his handicap debut over a trip he has never run over.

articles.title: Russell claims Dutch GP Sprint pole with Antonelli, Hamilton on back foot
articles.summary: George Russell made the ideal start to his attempt to mount a championship fightback in the second half of the 2026 F1 season by claiming pole position for Saturday's Dutch Grand Prix Sprint as nearest title rivals Kimi Antonelli and Lewis Hamilton qualified outside the top four.
body: On F1's first day back on track after the sport's four-week summer break, Russell claimed his third Sprint pole in five attempts this season as his final SQ3 lap of 1:11.567 beat McLaren's Lando Norris and Ferrari's Charles Leclerc to the head of the Zandvoort grid by under a tenth of a second.

But championship leader Antonelli was only fifth quickest in the other Mercedes, the Italian teenager's session compromised after he damaged his car in a trip through the gravel on his first lap of SQ1.
Hamilton, who is second to Antonelli in the standings, qualified only seventh in the second Ferrari after earlier promise on Friday faded.

Hamilton trails Antonelli by 50 points in the Drivers' Championship, with Russell a further nine points adrift. Points are on offer to the top-eight finishers in Saturday's 24-lap Sprint, which starts at 11am on Sky Sports F1, with eight for the winner.

videos.title: Preliminary Phase Draw for the FIFA Women’s World Cup 2027™ Play-Off Tournament
videos.summary: The preliminary phase for the Play-Off Tournament will take place in November and December 2026 at a centralised venue featuring six teams ranked based on the latest FIFA/Coca-Cola Women’s World Ranking prior to the play-off draw.
body: There will be two teams from the AFC, two from CAF, one from CONMEBOL and one from the OFC. Using a format which will be confirmed at a later date, two teams will qualify for the final play-off phase.

The final play-off phase will be played in a centralised location in February 2027, where the two qualifiers from the preliminary phase will be joined by two teams from Concacaf, one from CONMEBOL and one from UEFA.

The six teams will be drawn into three paths, with a direct knockout match to determine the final three teams qualifying for the FIFA Women’s World Cup 2027. Teams from the same confederation will not be permitted to be drawn in the same pathway.
